title: VLP RT-qPCR
author: Motoko Tanaka
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.k73czqn
materials: RNA co-­‐Immunoprecipitation By Motoko Tanaka and Brook Barajas in Jaisri Lingappa’s Laboratory, October 2017 Day 0: Plate Cells (for cos-­‐1 cells, split cell ~8hr before transfection) -­‐ COS-­‐1 cells: 6e5 cells/poly lysine-­‐coated 60m plate; 293T: 2e6 cells/60mm plate. -­‐ Use 4% lysate for TCL IP (=4.72x10^4 cell equivalent, 25 µL out of 620.5 µL lysate) Day 0: Transfect Cells 8 hours after plating cells, transfect each plate with desired plasmid(s). Before starting: • Label 1 1.5 mL Eppies per sample. • Thaw DNA at 55˚C in Thermomixer and rotate at >1000 RPM for 15 minutes to resuspend. • Thaw PEI (MANUFACTURER, CATALOGUE NUMBER) at 55˚C in Thermomixer and rotate at >1000 RPM for 15 minutes to resuspend. 1. For each transfection condition, dilute DNA in 500 µL pre-­‐warmed, serum-­‐free medium. 2. Let sit 5 minutes at room temperature (RT). 3. Add 20 µL of pre-­‐warmed PEI (more than 15min at 55˚C) to DNA/ serum-­‐media, incubate at RT 15 minutes. 4. Change media on cells to 3 mL of transfection media. 5. Add transfection mix dropwise to cells while gently rocking the plate. Day 1: Change media (when you culture cells more than 24 hrs after transfection) Before starting: • Warm PBS + MgCl2/CaCl2 • Warm culture media (for 293Ts and Cos-­‐1, 500 mLs DMEM + 10% FBS + 5 mLs penicillin/streptomycin) ~14 hours post transfection, rinse cells twice with 3 mL warmed PBS containing CaCl2 and MgCl2 to remove untransfected DNA, then add 3.5 mL fresh media. Day 2: HARVEST VLPs and lysate For COS-­‐1 cells, lysate and media should be harvested 34-­‐38 hours post-­‐transfection. For 293T cells, lysate and media should be harvested 15-­‐18 hours post-­‐transfection. Harvest VLPs (isolating VLPs from other particles in the supernatant): Before starting: • Label and pre-­‐chill 2 1.5 mL Eppies and 1 15 mL Falcon tube per sample. • Pre-­‐chill benchtop Allegra centrifuge to 4˚C. • Prepare 1.5 mLs of 30% sucrose per sample. • Make up 500 µL 1x NN+M with 1:100 Protease inhibitor (PI, MANUFACTURER, CATALOGUE NUMBER) and 1:1000 RNaseOUT per sample (MANUFACTURER, CATALOGUE NUMBER), chill (see end of protocol). • Obtain a 1 mL syringe and a 20-­‐guage needle for loading the sucrose cushion.

• Obtain 1 mL Trizol (Ambion, cat# 15590026) for each sample (make an aliquot of the needed volume + 10%, being careful not to draw from the bottom of the bottle). • Preheat RNA bench heat-­‐block or water bath to 55˚C. • Obtain 20 mg/mL Proteinase K (Sigma P4850). 1. Make up Proteinase K elution buffer To make 1 ml (for approx. 10 samples): 975 µL of non-­‐detergent 1x NN (see end of protocol) 15 µL Proteinase K 10 µL 10% SDS 2. a) TCL input: take 2.5 µL TCL out of total of 620.5 µL. b) VLPs: Take 2.5 µL VLPs out of total ~100 µL and mix with 7.5 µL 1xNN buffer. 3. Add Proteinase K elution buffer to 100 µL final volume. 4. Incubate at 55˚C for 30 minutes. 5. If water bath was used for incubation, dry tubes thoroughly. 6. Add 1 ml TRIZOL. Invert to mix well and incubate at RT for 5 minutes. -­‐ Store at -­‐80C if stopping. If you want to stop the experiment, stop at this point. RNA is not stable in isopropanol. Next stop point is the end of cDNA reaction. Day 3: RNA isolation and Reverse Transcription reaction RNA isolation with TRIZOL: Before starting RNA isolation and DNAse treatment: • Obtain 5 µL Glycoblue (Invitrogen AM9515 or AM9516) per sample. • Obtain 100 µL BCP (BP 151 phase separation reagent, Molecular Research Center, CATALOGUE NUMBER) per sample. • Prepare 0.7 mL of ice cold isopropanol per sample (store at -­‐20˚C until ready for use). • Prepare 1 mL of ice cold 75% ethanol per sample with PCR grade or DEPC-­‐treated water (store at -­‐20˚C until ready for use). • Prepare 51 µL of 1xDNase buffer (Invitrogen cat# 18068-­‐015) prepare with DEPC water) containing 1:1000 RNaseOut and 2U (1 µL) DNase (Invitrogen cat# 18068-­‐015) per sample. • Heat a clean-­‐room heat block or water bath to 25˚C. • Heat a clean-­‐room heat block or water bath to 65˚C. • Obtain 1.5 µL of 25mM EDTA per sample. • Pre-­‐chill an RNA-­‐designated centrifuge. • Clean benchtop, Pipetmen, and all equipment with RNase-­‐ZAP (MANUFACTURER, CATALOGUE NUMBER) or similar reagent. 1. If samples are frozen, thaw at room temperature and set on ice. Invert many times to promote lysis of material. 2. Spin down briefly to collect inverted liquid. 3. Add 75 μg of glycoblue (5 µL) and mix well by inverting tube. 4. Spin down briefly to collect inverted liquid. 5. Add 100 µL of BCP. 6. Vortex for 10-­‐15 seconds until emulsion forms, repeat 2 times. 7. Let sit on ice for 2-­‐3 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Reagents
steps.instruction: Pre-chill and prepare all necessary materials for VLP and lysate harvesting.

substeps.instruction: Label and pre-chill three 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes per sample.
Pre-chill benchtop Allegra centrifuge and microcentrifuge to 4°C.
Pre-chill 1 mL syringes with 20 gauge needles attached.
Prepare a cell scraper (aspirator pipette with rubber policeman scraper).
Thaw an aliquot of Puromycin (26.5 µL per sample); avoid multiple freeze-thaw cycles.
Prepare 144 µL of 2M KCl NN+M (high salt) per sample and keep chilled.

steps.title: Harvest and Filter VLP Supernatant
steps.instruction: Collect and clarify the supernatant containing VLPs.

substeps.instruction: Remove a plate of cells from the incubator and place on ice.
Collect supernatant into a 15 mL conical tube.
Spin supernatant at 2000 RPM for 7 min at 4°C.
Filter supernatant through a 0.45 µm pore size filter.

steps.title: Concentrate VLPs via Ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: Use a sucrose cushion to pellet the VLPs.

substeps.instruction: Add 2.7 mL of filtered supernatant into an ultracentrifuge tube.
Draw 1.5 mL of 30% (w/v) sucrose into a 1 mL syringe.
Slowly layer the sucrose underneath the filtered supernatant by placing the needle tip at the bottom of the tube.
Centrifuge at 60K RPM for 30 min at 4°C.
Slowly tilt the tube and suction the media and sucrose, avoiding the pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend VLP Fraction
steps.instruction: Recover the VLP pellet for further analysis.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL 30% sucrose to the pellet.
Vortex to resuspend and collect the VLP fraction into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Harvest and Lyse Cells
steps.instruction: Extract lysate from cells to release nascent chains.

substeps.instruction: Rinse cells twice with 3 mL ice-cold PBS containing CaCl2 and MgCl2.
Add 500 µL of 1x Lysis Buffer NN+M (supplemented with 1:100 Protease Inhibitor and 1:1000 RNaseOUT) per plate.
Scrape lysate and transfer to a chilled tube.
Shear lysed cells 20 times through a chilled 20-gauge needle.

steps.title: Clarify Lysate
steps.instruction: Remove cellular debris through sequential centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Spin lysed cells at 1000 RPM for 10 minutes at 4°C in a tabletop Allegra centrifuge.
Transfer the supernatant to a new tube.
Spin the supernatant at 14k RPM for 1 minute at 4°C in a microcentrifuge.
Transfer 450 µL of the resulting lysate to a new tube.

steps.title: Puromycin and High Salt Treatment
steps.instruction: Treat lysate to release RNA and stabilize the sample.

substeps.instruction: Warm lysate and Puromycin for 5 minutes at 26°C.
Add 26.5 µL Puromycin (18mM stock) to 450 µL lysate to reach a final concentration of 1mM.
Incubate for 10 minutes at 26°C.
Add 144 µL 2M high salt NN+M to reach a final concentration of 0.5M KCl (final volume 620.5 µL).
Incubate for 10 minutes at 26°C.
Place tubes on ice for at least 10 minutes.
Centrifuge at max speed for 1 min in a 4°C microcentrifuge.
Spin at 12,000xg for 15 minutes at 4°C in a chilled RNA-designated microcentrifuge.
Transfer 0.7 mL ice-cold isopropanol to a fresh labeled tube and keep on ice.
Transfer ~0.6 mL of the aqueous phase from the spun sample to the isopropanol tube.
Mix by inverting at least 5 times and store at -20°C for at least 1 hour.
Spin at 14K RPM for 30 minutes in a chilled centrifuge.
Remove supernatant using a 1 mL pipette, tilting the tube to avoid the pellet.
Wash pellet with 1 mL ice-cold 75% EtOH by inverting several times.
Spin at 14K RPM for 10 minutes in a chilled centrifuge.
Aspirate most EtOH, then spin at 14K RPM for 1 minute and remove remaining EtOH with a P200 pipette.
Move samples to a clean room and allow RNA pellets to air dry for ~3 minutes, closing the tube before they over-dry.

steps.title: DNase I Treatment
steps.instruction: Remove contaminating DNA from the RNA sample.

substeps.instruction: Add 51 µL of 1x DNase buffer (DEPC water) containing 1:1000 RNaseOut and 2U DNase (1 µL) by sliding the liquid down the sidewall onto the pellet.
Tap to resuspend, spin briefly, and mix by pipetting 5 times (running liquid over the sidewall).
Incubate at 25°C for 15 minutes.
Add 1.5 µL of 25mM EDTA, mix, and spin.
Heat sample at 65°C for 10 minutes to inactivate DNase I.

steps.title: cDNA Synthesis (RT Reaction)
steps.instruction: Convert isolated RNA into cDNA using the iScript Advanced cDNA synthesis kit.

substeps.instruction: Pre-heat water bath to 42°C and heat block to 85°C.
Prepare cDNA master mix: 10 µL PCR grade H2O, 4 µL 5X Script reaction mix, and 1 µL 20X RT enzyme mix.
For +RT and -RNA control: Aliquot 15 µL master mix and add 5 µL RNA (or 5 µL DEPC H2O for -RNA control).
For RT- controls: Mix 15 µL PCR grade H2O and 5 µL RNA.
Incubate samples at 42°C for 30 minutes in the water bath.
Incubate samples at 85°C for 5 minutes in the heat block.
Dilute cDNA 1:3 by adding 51 µL DEPC H2O to 17 µL cDNA; store at -80°C or proceed to qPCR.

steps.title: Prepare qPCR Oligos and Standards
steps.instruction: Prepare primers and a standard curve outside the clean room.

substeps.instruction: Dilute oligos to 200 µM, mix forward and reverse 1:1 to make 100 µM stock, then dilute to 10 µM for use.
Prepare initial standard dilution of 1e8 copies/2 µl in 20 µL aliquots (store at -80°C).
Create a 1:10 dilution series from 1e1 to 1e8 copies/2 µL by adding 5 µL of the previous dilution to 45 µL DEPC water.

steps.title: qPCR Plate Setup and Run
steps.instruction: Set up the qPCR reaction and run the thermal cycling program.

substeps.instruction: Prepare qPCR mix: 9.75 µL DEPC water, 12.5 µL 2x SYBR Green (cat# 170-8884), and 0.75 µL 10 µM oligo mix.
Prepare duplicate reactions in Eppendorf tubes, then aliquot into a 96-well plate.
Add 2 µL of 4-fold diluted cDNA to sample wells.
Load 2 µL of each standard per well in duplicate (top two rows).
Seal plate with foil and centrifuge briefly at 500 RPM.
Run qPCR program: 95°C (30s), then 35 cycles of [95°C (15s), 60°C (15s), 72°C (30s + 10s collection)], followed by 55°C (1 min) and 55°C Tm measurement.
